messages:
Raj Patel: :rotating_light: seeing widespread GPU allocation failures in eu-west2 - nvlink errors and a spike in KV-cache misses since ~1971234500. Pool health on affected AZs is down to ~40% available.
ops-bot: Autoscaler triggered + created ticket INC-2026-498 (investigating).
Emily Chen: Are we on the automatic failover policy? If so we should start shifting non-pinned traffic to us-west1 asap.
Chris Gomez: don’t blast everything over — a lot of customers pin to eu regions. Recommend a staged shift: 70% to us-west1, 20% keep local for pinned customers, 10% canary to eu-west1-secondary.
Maria Lopez: I’ll start drafting the status page and ping enterprise contacts. Suggested short message: "We are investigating GPU allocation failures and elevated latency in eu-west2. Some workloads may fail to schedule; we are shifting traffic and expect mitigation within ~45m." Thoughts? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Emily Chen: note — using burst capacity in us-west1 will hit overage pricing for some Dedicated customers. We should flag billing ops and add an ETA for cost review if we need to keep the shift longer than 2h.
Oliver Wang: taking affected nodes out of rotation now.
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42.eu-west2
kubectl drain gpu-node-42.eu-west2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# observed kernel logs: "nvlink: remote link down" repeated
```
Raj Patel: rolling the staged routing now. Applying 70% -> us-west1, 20% stickiness to pinned, 10% canary. Will update status page and start a performance watch.
Chris Gomez: routing command I’m running for the canary:
```bash
red-ctl routing apply --from eu-west2 --to us-west1 --percent 70 --canary 10m
```
incident-bridge: Bridge created: https://bridges.internal/1971234567 - dial-in + chat open.
Maria Lopez: Posting status page update draft to #status-updates: 
"We are investigating issues impacting GPU allocations and latency in eu-west2 caused by a networking partition affecting NVLink/KV cache. We have initiated a staged traffic shift to us-west1 and are cordoning affected hosts. Estimated mitigation: 45 minutes. Customers with pinned resources remain available where possible; enterprise contacts have been notified. We will update at 15-minute intervals or on major milestones."
Raj Patel: tagging #support-urgent if any customers escalate. If we see errors drop and allocations recover we’ll start shifting traffic back with a 10m canary first.
Emily Chen: monitor cost impact and keep financeLoop in the thread if we keep cross-region burst beyond 2 hours.
ops-bot: Incident status changed -> "Mitigating".
